about: The bones of the hip and thigh as an anatomy textbook draws them: the hip bones, their joints and the femurs, following the femoral vessels to the point where the glass leg fades. Bone is not simulated as tissue, so no part has a live drive. This is a first-pass schematic: the parts are named and listed, and their drawing is still to come.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Hip Bones
parts.summary: Two broad bones of the pelvis
parts.function: Each hip bone is the fusion of three bones, the ilium, ischium and pubis. Together with the sacrum they form the pelvic ring that carries the weight of the trunk and protects the pelvic organs.

parts.label: Femora
parts.summary: Thigh bones, the longest bones in the body
parts.function: Each femur runs from the hip joint to the knee. Its rounded head sits in the hip socket and its lower end forms the thigh side of the knee joint.

parts.label: Hip Joints
parts.summary: Ball-and-socket joints between femur and hip bone
parts.function: The head of the femur fits into the cup-shaped acetabulum of the hip bone. The joint carries the body's weight and allows movement in every direction.

parts.label: Pubic Symphysis
parts.summary: Joint at the front of the pelvis
parts.function: The two pubic bones meet at the midline in a cartilage joint that allows very little movement.
